description: Computing node J and cold plate C of the thermal design against the ISS finite element cold-plate equipment (MBSU, DDCU, IEA) of the mean environment case nom0. Values under case_inputs are the inputs of the FE-003 entry of Thermal/test_report/build_test_report_cn.py; the test checks them against the FE model parameter table iss_fem/model/iss_spec.py and takes the values used in the runs from that table and from the FE results.

fe.source: ISS FE model, COMSOL 6.3, report iss_fem/docs/REPORT.md sections 3.6 (block heat sources: uniform volume heat, one face on a convective cold-plate boundary to the 2.8 C NH3 supply), 3.8 (orbit noon to 16560 s, statistics over the last 5553.6 s), 5.1 table 12 and 5.4 table 17; items.csv Tmean_C is the mean over the orbit 3 output samples of the volume average (iss_fem/model/iss_solve.py), loop_breakdown.csv W_mean the mean over the same samples of the cold-plate heat of each loop group

case_inputs.remainder_note: The case text attributes the remainder of about 5.4 percent to the MLI. The FE writes the cold-plate heat per loop, not per MBSU or DDCU; the test compares the loop remainder (block heat minus loop cold-plate heat) with 5.4 percent and does not split it. In the FE the remainder holds the radiation of the MLI outer faces of the blocks (iss_spec OPTICS box: absorptivity 0.012, emissivity 0.03; blocks sit 0.05 m off the truss faces, ORU_BOXES) and the heat still stored in blocks that warm through the third orbit.
case_inputs.source: CASES['FE-003'] input and steps of Thermal/test_report/build_test_report_cn.py: MBSU 495 W 0.79 m2, DDCU 694 W 0.56 m2, IEA 6000 W 13.5 m2, cold-plate conductance 60 W/m2K, equivalent conductivity 150 W/mK, coolant 2.8 C, about 5.4 percent of the block heat leaves through the MLI, conduction length one third of the device thickness

rounding.note: case values are written with the digits of the case text; the FE values must round to them

compute_node.range_source: FE-003 test configuration: the FE uses constant properties for the equivalent solid oru_eq (iss_spec MATERIALS); the declared range covers the temperatures of the runs
compute_node.initial_temperature_source: FE initial temperature of the external ORU and IEA blocks, iss_spec T_INIT['box'] = 285 K (FE report 3.8)

cold_plate.source: FE-003 precondition recorded per thermal design 9.4: the cold plate takes a very large capacitance, starts at the coolant temperature and CR takes a very large resistance, so the cold-plate temperature stays at the coolant temperature like the FE cold-plate boundary (convective boundary to the fixed NH3 supply set point, FE report 3.7 and 3.9 item 5)

auxiliary_nodes.note: S, B, D and R are not compared in FE-003. Their explicit values only complete the six-node model; P_pv_W, Q_B_W and Q_D_W are zero and CR decouples the cold plate from R.
auxiliary_nodes.source: FE-003 auxiliary node, not compared; explicit test value

environment.resolution_note: Earth albedo and infrared of the auxiliary S and R surfaces from sdtwin_sim.earth_flux with a 120 by 180 grid; J and C have no exposed surface (design 4.4) and do not use these inputs
environment.attitude: body +Z points at the Sun at every instant; body +X along the orbit normal component perpendicular to the Sun line
environment.epoch_note: nominal UTC epoch; the FE environment is fixed by beta and the case values, not by a date

solver.source: thermal design table 8: adaptive RK45 with relative tolerance, temperature absolute tolerance and maximum step as scene settings; maximum step equal to the 120 s step of the FE; output sampled on the accepted solution every 60 s

run.note: integration to steady state: 14 FE orbital periods from orbit noon; the slowest device, the IEA, has C_J R_JC of about 8.7e3 s, so the initial difference decays by a factor of about 7e3 or more

criteria.source: acceptance 1 K from CASES['FE-003']; the steady-state and exponential tolerance 0.001 K follow the analytic cases of HT-003; the relative tolerance 1e-12 follows PA-001 and HT-002
